correctness.rationale: Normalize the distinct unique winners to PAV=AB and CC=AC. Let a,b,c be singleton counts and x,y,z be counts for AB, AC, BC. CC compares the singleton counts of the omitted candidates, so b<a,c. Twice the PAV score difference AB−AC is 2(b−c)+x−y; strictness forces x−y≥3. Thus n≥a+c+x≥2b+5. Equality forces b=0, a=c=1, x=3, and all other ballot counts zero, including empty and full ballots. Direct scores (11/2,5,4) and (4,5,4) give both strict winners, including the comparison with BC. The stabilizer is trivial: C is outside the repeated doubleton, and A is its uniquely singled-out member. There are six candidate renamings and 20 voter labelings each. Independent exact labeled and multinomial-weighted anonymous enumeration confirmed 0,0,0,0,120 conflicts for n=1 through 5, 11,970 jointly unique labeled profiles at n=5, and six conflicts among 792 anonymous profiles. The reported three fractions reduce exactly. This does not bound disagreement through ties or address other candidate and committee sizes.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive evidence applies only to the stated all-eight-ballot, three-candidate, two-seat domain.

value.rationale: Three candidates and two seats is the smallest geometry in which two multiwinner committees can compete. The two established representation objectives handle one approved member identically and differ on their treatment of two; isolating the first strict reversal therefore separates a real rule difference from tie handling. The characterization gives a reusable minimal witness and the exact incidence distinguishes the size of the disagreement set from the size of its jointly resolute domain. This is a narrow exact benchmark, not a general performance claim.
residual_risks: The uniform finite-domain frequencies are not estimates for structured electorates or other ballot distributions.
